report:
# Cranberry Juice/Extract for Preventing Recurrent Cystitis in Women: Mixed and Modest Evidence

**Bottom line: The evidence is inconsistent and generally weak, so "yes" is an oversimplification.** Some trials in adult women show benefit, but the most rigorous systematic review (Cochrane) and head-to-head antibiotic comparisons suggest cranberry products offer limited, if any, meaningful protection against recurrent UTIs/cystitis.

**The case for benefit:** Early studies specifically in adult women found cranberry juice reduced UTI recurrences (as referenced in the trial cited by [PMC3060891](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3060891/), which notes "cranberry juice prevents recurrences of urinary tract infections (UTIs) in adult women"). A more recent meta-analysis reported that cranberry-containing products "may protect against UTIs in certain populations," particularly women with recurrent infections ([medicalxpress.com](https://medicalxpress.com/news/2012-07-cranberry-products-urinary-tract-infections.html)).

**The case against/for caution:** The authoritative Cochrane systematic review found that cranberry juice is "unlikely to prevent" bladder and kidney infections, reversing earlier positive conclusions after including larger, better-designed trials ([sciencedaily.com](https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2012/10/121016204143.htm)). A randomized noninferiority trial in premenopausal women found that antibiotics (TMP-SMX) were significantly more effective than cranberry capsules at preventing recurrent UTIs, though cranberries avoided antibiotic resistance risks ([cris.maastrichtuniversity.nl](https://cris.maastrichtuniversity.nl/en/publications/cranberries-vs-antibiotics-to-prevent-urinary-tract-infections-a-/)).

**Conclusion:** Effects appear population-specific and generally modest at best. Cranberry products are not a proven, reliable substitute for established prevention strategies, though they may offer minor benefit for some women wanting to avoid antibiotics. The "yes" answer is not well-supported by the strongest available evidence.
